requirement: Define/implement changed_since,cursor,removed tombstones/exclusions and corpusVersion; dataRev is explicitly not a durable change feed.

protocol.order: (updatedAt, _id) ascending with an opaque cursor; page limit as the snapshot's
protocol.items: A corpus row exactly as a snapshot item; a row that left the corpus as {gameId, removed: true}.
protocol.watermark: max(since, first page time - 5 min) on the final page; rows near it may repeat.
protocol.snapshotMarks: The snapshot's first page carries corpusVersion and its watermark, read before the page.
protocol.corpusVersion: users.corpusVersion, bumped before and after the hard delete in the history wipe, in restore and in account erasure, and again when the delete throws partway.
protocol.stampFloor: A durable siteConfig floor created when the service is built at boot, 7 minutes ahead, and cached per process; a before_stamps answer carries deltasFrom = floor + 5 min.
protocol.validation: The query is validated before the single corpus lane is taken; a since more than 60 s ahead is refused.

fixed: Medium: withCorpusRemoval skipped the second version bump whenever the delete threw partway, and a batched delete can throw after earlier batches committed. It now bumps on that path too and reports the delete's error (util/corpusUpdatedAt.js:50-57).

Medium: the stamp floor was created by the first changes request, so for about 12 minutes after AC3's launch every delta would have needed a snapshot that could not yet succeed. The floor is now created when the service is built at boot and cached in-process, and a before_stamps answer carries deltasFrom (services/analysisCorpusChanges.js:27-53,77).

Low-medium: account erasure's games delete did not bump the version, so an erasure that failed after it left the device's rows at an unchanged version. It now runs inside withCorpusRemoval (services/gdpr.js:444-452).
Low: a changes query was validated after it took the single corpus lane. It is now validated first (routes/games.js:110).
Low: a since in the future froze the watermark. One more than 60 s ahead is refused (services/analysisCorpusChanges.js:110-116).
documented: Low: a rollback below AC1 leaves the floor in the past while unstamped rows land. The checkpoint says to raise the floor before rolling forward again.
Info: during a rolling deploy, a process from before AC2 answers 404 on /changes and sends first snapshot pages without marks. AC3 must treat both as snapshot only.
A process crash between a hard delete and its second bump, with a snapshot taken in that window, can still leave that device stale until its next snapshot.
testGapsClosed: A wipe that throws after deleting, and an erasure that throws after its games delete, still bump twice.
A row stamped before a pass ended but committed after it comes back from the returned watermark.
Concurrent first stamp-floor reads agree on one floor.
A since in the future is refused.
A delta waits for the snapshot's corpus permit, and malformed input is refused while the lane is held.
notAdopted: An owner-bound version token: re-provisioning after a successful erasure creates a new random owner id (services/users.js:74), so a reset version cannot be read as the old account's continuity.

Separate abort tests for the delta route: both routes run through one page handler, the admission queue and permit hold it uses have unit tests, and the delta route's use of the shared lane now has a route test.
independentReview.note: One read-only reviewer covered missed changes, the stamp floor, the route refactor, owner scoping and test gaps. Owner scoping was clean.

boundaries: No web client uses the route yet; AC3 adds the device store. The item stays partial.
A process crash between a hard delete and its second version bump, with a snapshot in that window, can leave that device stale until its next snapshot.
During a rolling deploy a process from before AC2 answers 404 on /changes and sends first snapshot pages without marks; AC3 must treat both as snapshot only.
A rollback below AC1 needs the floor raised to the redeploy time plus 7 minutes before rolling forward again.
Exact-head CI, merge, deployment and production acceptance remain pending. No latency, request-reduction or savings claim.
